;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]; [[May 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**In [[Kabul]], gunmen wearing police uniforms [[mass shooting|open fire]], killing at least 24 people, including two newborns, in the [[maternity ward]] of a hospital. Security forces kill the attackers. In [[Kuz Kunar District|Kuz Kunar]], a [[suicide bomber]] kills at least 32 people at a funeral. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-52642503 (BBC News)]
**In response, [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] orders that the [[Afghan Armed Forces|armed forces]] switch to the "offensive" and to "start operations against the enemy". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-security/afghan-president-orders-troops-to-switch-to-offensive-stance-after-attacks-idUSKBN22O2CN (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**An [[Israel Defense Forces]] soldier dies after being struck on the head by [[stone throwing|a thrown stone]] in the [[West Bank]] town of [[Ya'bad]]. The military is seeking a suspect. In a separate incident, [[Israeli police]] in [[Kalandia]] shoot and wound a [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] man attempting to stab officers. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-israel-palestinians-violence/palestinian-rock-thrower-kills-israeli-soldier-in-west-bank-military-idUKKBN22O13K (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least five [[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia|COVID-19 patients]] in a hospital in [[Vyborgsky District, Saint Petersburg|Vyborgsky District]], [[St. Petersburg]], [[Russia]], die after a [[ventilator]] caught fire in the [[intensive care]] ward they are treated in. [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-ventilator-fire-in-st-petersburg-hospital-kills-covid-19-patients/a-53400972 (DW)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Kremlin]] [[Kremlin Press Secretary|Press Secretary]] [[Dmitry Peskov]] is hospitalized after testing positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://apnews.com/0e8858138ffa9082bff09b960a3217ce (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Government of Brazil|Brazil]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Brazil)|Ministry of Health]] reports 881 more deaths from COVID-19, the highest daily death toll in the country to date, bringing the country's death toll to 12,400 and 177,589 total cases. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-52644339 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[China–Australia relations]]; [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[Government of China|China]] suspends imports of beef from four Australian [[abattoir]]s, saying that its customs agency "continuously" found violations of inspection and [[quarantine]] requirements. Foreign ministry spokesman [[Zhao Lijian]] says the suspension comes to "ensure the safety and health of Chinese consumers". This comes after the [[Government of Australia|Australian government]] last month called for an independent inquiry into the origins of the [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|novel coronavirus]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-australia-china-beef/china-suspends-imports-from-four-australian-abattoirs-as-ties-sour-trade-idUSKBN22O0FB (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Forest of Dean unidentified body]]
**A man and woman are arrested in the [[Forest of Dean]] in connection with the discovery of the remains of a woman found in two suitcases. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/may/14/inquiry-launched-after-human-remains-found-in-forest-of-dean (''The Guardian'')]
